analysis.title: USA: Core Producer Prices Increase in Line With Expectations and PCE-Relevant PPI Components Softer; Estimating 0.30% for October
key_insights: October PPI rose 0.3% MoM (+6.5% YoY), in line with GS at +0.3% and below the median forecast of +0.4%. The prior month was revised to +1.4%.
Core PPI (ex-food and energy) rose 0.3% MoM (+5.0% YoY), in line with the median forecast of +0.3% and above GS at +0.2%. The prior month was revised to +0.8%.
PPI ex-food, energy, and trade services rose 0.5% MoM (+4.9% YoY), above GS at +0.3% and the median forecast of +0.4%. The prior month was also +0.5%.
Energy PPI fell 0.1% after sharp increases in the prior two months tied to the re-escalation of the conflict in Iran.
Retailer margins fell 0.2% after a September reading that was the largest monthly increase since March 2022.
The 'old methodology' core PPI (finished goods ex-food and energy) rose 0.3%. Core intermediate prices rose 0.9%, and crude materials ex-food and energy fell 0.9%, the first decline since June.
PCE-relevant PPI components were on net softer than GS expected. Domestic passenger airfares fell 1.8% (seasonally adjusted by GS) after sharp increases in August and September.
Medical care PPI categories relevant for PCE were mixed but on net weaker than GS expected. GS estimates PCE medical care services rose 0.14% MoM in October.
After the PPI and CPI details, GS estimates October core PCE rose 0.30% MoM (vs. 0.35% expected before the PPI), or +3.24% YoY.
GS expects headline PCE rose 0.32% MoM in October and 3.83% YoY.

macro_indicators.reading: +0.3% MoM, +6.5% YoY (vs. GS +0.3%, median forecast +0.4%, prior revised +1.4%)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Headline producer prices cooled sharply from the prior month's +1.4% as energy turned slightly negative, and came in a touch below consensus.

macro_indicators.reading: +0.3% MoM, +5.0% YoY (vs. GS +0.2%, median forecast +0.3%, prior revised +0.8%)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Core producer prices matched consensus and slowed from the prior month's +0.8%.

macro_indicators.reading: +0.5% MoM, +4.9% YoY (vs. GS +0.3%, median forecast +0.4%, prior +0.5%)
macro_indicators.interpretation: The measure that strips out retailer and wholesaler margins was slightly hotter than expected, so underlying producer cost pressure has not eased.
Energy prices dipped after sharp gains in the prior two months tied to the re-escalation of the Iran conflict.
Margins fell after September's largest monthly increase since March 2022, which pulled down the trade services component.

macro_indicators.indicator: PPI domestic passenger airfares (seasonally adjusted by GS)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Airfares fell after sharp increases in August and September, a softer input into the PCE price index.

macro_indicators.reading: +0.30% MoM, +3.24% YoY (vs. GS pre-PPI expectation of 0.35%)
macro_indicators.interpretation: GS cut its October core PCE estimate by 5bp after the PPI and CPI details. The official PCE release has not yet been published.
GS expects headline PCE to run slightly above core in October.
Built from PPI and interim PPI data that GS seasonally adjusts. It is weaker than GS expected and helps lower the core PCE estimate.

geopolitical: Energy prices rose sharply in the two months before October, reflecting the re-escalation of the conflict in Iran.
